title: SwitchTop-$k$: Scaling Top-$k$ Compression on Programmable Switches

problem.claim: Large-scale distributed training requires reducing gradient data volume to reduce training time.

gap.claim: Existing Top-k compression solutions are inefficient for large-scale distributed training because of gradient build-up, missing Top-k gradients, and high end-host compression overhead.

contributions.claim: SwitchTop-k offloads Top-k compression from end hosts to programmable switches.
SwitchTop-k uses a sketch-based solution to select global Top-k gradients with high accuracy.
The system co-designs switch logic and end-host logic to improve communication efficiency for uncompressed traffic.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report implementing SwitchTop-k on Intel Tofino switches and integrating it with PyTorch.
The authors report that SwitchTop-k reduces iteration time by up to 91% compared with existing compression algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Distributed deep learning is widely deployed in data centers, and Top-k compression is used to reduce gradient data volume.
Existing Top-k compression solutions are inefficient at large scale because of gradient build-up, missing Top-k gradients, and end-host compression overhead.
SwitchTop-k moves compression to programmable switches and combines high-accuracy Top-k selection with high compression and zero compression overhead.
The method co-designs switch and end-host logic to improve communication efficiency for uncompressed traffic.
SwitchTop-k is implemented on Intel Tofino switches with PyTorch, and the authors report up to 91% lower iteration time than existing compression algorithms.

unknowns: The abstract does not report accuracy impact or the evaluation workload configuration.
The abstract does not describe the specific causes or frequency of missing Top-k gradients.
The abstract does not provide absolute iteration times, compression rates, or comparison baselines.
